WHY: HTTP statusText is not guaranteed to be the literal "OK" across proxies, localized servers, or HTTP/2, so successful token responses can be falsely rejected. HOW: Use `if (!response.ok)` or `if (response.status !== 200)` instead.

WHAT: The webhook secret is validated with the `!==` operator. WHY: `!==` short-circuits on the first mismatch and leaks timing information that an attacker on the network could use to guess the secret byte-by-byte. HOW: Use a constant-time comparison such as `crypto.timingSafeEqual` after lowercasing and converting both values to equal-length Buffers.

WHAT: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws when parsing fails, so `parsedToken.success` is always true after the call returns. WHY: The `if (!parsedToken.success)` branch that follows in Zoom (and the equivalent branch in Salesforce) is unreachable and gives a false impression of graceful error handling. HOW: Remove the unreachable check, or change parseRefreshTokenResponse to return the SafeParseReturnType without throwing so callers can branch on success.

WHAT: GoogleCalendarService stores the entire Zod SafeParseReturnType object as the credential key. WHY: The next read of credential.key will see { success: true, data: { ... } } instead of the raw Google credentials, breaking calendar API calls and subsequent token refreshes. HOW: Use parseRefreshTokenResponse(...).data as the key value.

WHAT: biginAuth passes credential.id to refreshOAuthTokens's userId parameter. WHY: The credential-sync endpoint receives calcomUserId=<credential ID>, so it may refresh or return tokens for the wrong principal. HOW: Pass credential.userId instead of credentialId.

WHAT: refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response when CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is configured, but returns the refreshFunction's typed result otherwise. WHY: Zoho Bigin, Zoho CRM, and Hubspot callers assume axios/SDK response shapes (e.g., .data.error, .data.access_token, .expiresIn, .accessToken) and will throw or write NaN/undefined values when the sync branch returns a fetch Response. HOW: Normalize the sync-endpoint response to the same shape the callers expect, or have callers explicitly handle the Response branch.

optimize-header-layout-performance-with-.texto: WHAT: `.d-header .contents` is now a flex container, but the header template still applies the `clearfix` class, whose `::before`/`::after` pseudo-elements use `display: table`. WHY: In a flex formatting context those pseudo-elements become flex items, so they participate in the header layout, create extra gaps before/after the real content, and can be reordered among children because `.panel` and `.extra-info-wrapper` use explicit `order` values. HOW: Remove the `clearfix` class from the `.contents` div in `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/header.hbs`, since `.contents` no longer needs float containment.

WHAT: `.small-action` is now a flex container, but `.small-action-desc` is left as a default `flex: 0 1 auto` flex item with no width. WHY: With short description text the description box shrinks to its content width, so the `float: right` delete/edit buttons inside it no longer align to the right edge of the action row as they did when the block-level description spanned the full width. HOW: Add `flex: 1;` to `.small-action-desc` so it occupies the remaining flex space and the floated buttons stay right-aligned.

optimize-spans-buffer-insertion-with-evi.texto: WHAT: zunionstore merges sorted-set scores with the default AGGREGATE SUM, so when a span payload exists in both source and destination sets its end_timestamp_precise score is doubled. WHY: Duplicate spans or hierarchy merges now appear newer than they are and are incorrectly protected from eviction, breaking the oldest-first eviction contract. HOW: Add AGGREGATE MAX to both zunionstore calls so the member keeps a single valid end timestamp.

WHAT: SpansBuffer still accepts and stores max_segment_spans, but the only consumer (the span-count guard in _load_segment_data) was removed and the Lua script hardcodes 1000. WHY: Changing the constructor argument now has no effect, so operators can silently misconfigure the eviction limit. HOW: Either remove the unused parameter or pass the limit to the Lua script and use it instead of the hardcoded 1000.

WHAT: zpopmin evicts members with the lowest end_timestamp_precise scores regardless of whether a span is the segment root or an ancestor. WHY: A root span that ends before one of its descendants can be evicted, so flush_segments later builds and emits a segment whose is_segment root span is missing. HOW: Track the root span's member (or span_id) separately and exclude it from zpopmin, or add a secondary hierarchy-based score so ancestors rank higher.

WHAT: zpopmin evicts the spans with the lowest end_timestamp_precise scores without protecting the segment root. WHY: the root span can be removed from its own segment set while has_root_span_key stays true, so flush_segments emits an incomplete segment and uses the shorter root-span timeout. HOW: encode hierarchy in the sorted-set score (e.g., a tier boost for root/segment spans) or store root spans in a separate, non-evicted key.

WHAT: zunionstore uses the default AGGREGATE SUM, so a span payload present in both source sets gets a score equal to the sum of its end timestamps. WHY: duplicate or redelivered spans corrupt the sorted-set score, breaking the oldest-first eviction invariant. HOW: pass AGGREGATE MAX so duplicate members keep the maximum (latest) end_timestamp_precise.

WHAT: SpansBuffer still accepts max_segment_spans, but the only production usage was removed and the Lua script hardcodes 1000. WHY: callers that configure a different limit silently get the hardcoded behavior, breaking the constructor contract. HOW: pass max_segment_spans as an argument to the Lua script and use it as the eviction threshold instead of 1000, or remove the option entirely.

plugins-chore-renamed-instrumentation-mi.texto: WHAT: TestLogger.FromContext returns a freshly allocated TestLogger, so log calls issued through the contextual logger are not captured by the original fake. WHY: Tests that pass a TestLogger to code using logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...) will see no calls on the injected logger, breaking assertions and making the fake unreliable for contextual logging. HOW: Return f itself (or a derived TestLogger that shares the same Logs structs) from FromContext so logs remain observable.

replays-self-serve-bulk-delete-system-se.texto: WHAT: The mutually-exclusive `timestamp`/`age` validators use truthy `self.initial_data.get(...)` checks instead of presence checks. WHY: A report containing both fields is accepted when either value is 0 (e.g., `timestamp=0` and `age=0`), violating the W3C reporting spec's mutual exclusivity and producing silently invalid data. HOW: Replace `self.initial_data.get("age")` with `"age" in self.initial_data` and `self.initial_data.get("timestamp")` with `"timestamp" in self.initial_data`.

WHAT: `fetch_error_details` pairs `error_ids` with `nodestore.backend.get_multi(...).values()` via `zip`. WHY: `get_multi` returns only found node IDs, so when any error event is missing from nodestore the remaining values shift and get attached to the wrong error IDs (or are dropped), sending incorrect error context to the AI summary. HOW: Iterate `(event_id, node_id)` pairs together and look up each `node_id` in the returned dict, e.g. `events.get(node_id)`.

WHAT: When the `use-table-widget-visualization` feature flag is enabled, `tableResultComponent` renders `TableWidgetVisualization` with hardcoded empty `columns` and `tableData`. WHY: Any dashboard table widget rendered under this flag will display no rows and no columns regardless of the actual query results. HOW: Pass the real `fields`, `result.data`, and `result.meta` (or derive `TabularColumn`s from `fields`) instead of the empty placeholder.

WHAT: The serializer accepts reports that omit both `age` and `timestamp` because each field is `required=False` and no cross-field validator requires at least one. WHY: A browser report with neither field is invalid under both the Working Draft and Editor's Draft specs, but the endpoint returns 200 and records a metric. HOW: Add a `validate` method (or keep the existing field validators and add a top-level check) that rejects data unless exactly one of `age` or `timestamp` is present.

sms-workflow-reminder-retry-count-tracki.texto: WHAT: The deleteMany cleanup predicate deletes every WorkflowReminder with retryCount greater than 1, not just SMS reminders. WHY: retryCount is added to the shared WorkflowReminder model, so email or future method reminders that ever reach retryCount > 1 are silently deleted by an SMS-specific cron job. HOW: Add method: WorkflowMethods.SMS to the retryCount branch of the OR clause.

WHAT: The catch block increments retryCount for any error in the whole try body, including after a successful Twilio schedule when only the scheduled=true DB update fails. WHY: A reminder can be retried and eventually deleted while Twilio still holds a scheduled message, causing orphan Twilio messages and lost reminders. HOW: Only increment retryCount when the scheduling call itself fails, and handle DB persistence errors separately.

WHAT: The cleanup deleteMany adds OR(retryCount > 1) but the WorkflowReminder table has no index on retryCount. WHY: PostgreSQL may fall back to a sequential scan for the retryCount branch, making the cron cleanup slower as the table grows. HOW: Add an index on retryCount, or combine method and retryCount in a composite index so the OR branches can both use indexes.

span-buffer-multiprocess-enhancement-wit.texto: WHAT: join(timeout) breaks out of the process loop when the deadline expires before every process is visited. WHY: Child processes that have not yet been iterated are left running as orphaned processes instead of being terminated, leaking resources and continuing to flush after the consumer shutdown path has given up. HOW: Always terminate each process even when the deadline has passed, e.g. by moving the terminate() call outside the deadline-guarded wait block.

WHAT: Metrics tags use 'shard' for spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes, but 'shards' for spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce. WHY: Dashboards and alerts that group by 'shard' will silently miss the wait_produce timing, and vice versa. HOW: Use the same tag key for all three metrics, e.g. 'shard'.

WHAT: submit() calls buffer.get_memory_info() for every per-process buffer, and each buffer points to the same Redis cluster. WHY: This multiplies Redis INFO calls by the number of flusher processes on every submit, increasing load without improving accuracy because the same cluster memory is reported each time. HOW: Collect memory info once from any buffer (or deduplicate by node) instead of summing across all buffers.

WHAT: join(timeout) breaks out of the process shutdown loop as soon as the shared deadline expires, so any processes after that index are never terminated. WHY: If next_step.join(timeout) consumes the full timeout or an earlier process drains the remainder, the remaining flusher child processes are left running, contradicting the graceful-shutdown intent and risking incomplete flushes or orphaned workers. HOW: Remove the remaining_time <= 0 break so the loop visits every process and calls terminate() even when the deadline has passed, matching the original single-process behavior.

WHAT: submit() calls record_stored_segments() and get_memory_info() once per flusher process instead of once total. WHY: Each per-process buffer shares the same Redis cluster, so the parent now issues num_processes redundant Redis pipelines and cluster.info() calls on every submit, scaling main-thread overhead linearly with the flusher process count the PR is trying to increase. HOW: Keep the original full-shard buffer (or a single parent buffer) and call record_stored_segments() and get_memory_info() on it once, instead of looping over self.buffers.values().

unified-storage-performance-optimization.texto: WHAT: Removing the function-level cacheMu lock allows concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same NamespacedResource to create duplicate indexes. WHY: Two concurrent Search requests for an uncached resource both pass getOrCreateIndex's nil check and enter BuildIndex, so both allocate/build indexes and the second cache write overwrites the first; for file-backed indexes both goroutines create or write the same directory. HOW: Add a per-key build lock (for example, a sync.Map of *sync.Mutex keyed by NamespacedResource) so only one goroutine builds a given key while others wait and reuse the cached result.

WHAT: When NewResourceServer calls s.Init and initialization fails, it returns nil without invoking the server's cancel function. WHY: The caller has no server handle to stop, so the context.WithCancel goroutine created at line 229 and any watcher goroutines started before the failure are leaked. HOW: Call s.cancel() before returning the error.

ux-show-complete-url-path-if-website-dom.texto: WHAT: website_name is serialized for TL0 users viewed anonymously even though website is hidden. WHY: the attribute is missing from untrusted_attributes and the custom include_website_name guard only checks website.present?, leaking the user's website domain/path to anonymous viewers. HOW: add :website_name to the untrusted_attributes list and rename or remove include_website_name so the generated include_website_name? method respects restrict_user_fields?.

WHAT: website_name parses URI(website.to_s) up to four times. WHY: each branch re-parses the same URL to read the path, wasting CPU on every user profile serialization. HOW: parse once into a local variable and reuse its host and path.

WHAT: the same-length subdomain branch treats domains sharing a public suffix as related. WHY: comparing labels [1..-1] makes foo.co.uk and bar.co.uk match, incorrectly exposing the full website path when the instance is on a different domain under the same public suffix. HOW: compare only the single label immediately below the public suffix, or use a public-suffix library to find the registered domain before matching.
